name: pub style lentils
instructions:
PUB STYLE LENTILS — the anglo-dark lentil stew. Merged (2026-11-02) from the former LENTIL COTTAGE PIE (the cumin + marmite line) and MUSHROOM PICKLE RELISH (the ale + pickle line): one recipe, TWO BUILDS sharing one register and ONE BITTER-ANCHOR SLOT — MARMITE (the buffered build, served on mash) or DARK ALE (the spare build, pickle tang). NEVER STACK ANCHORS. See [[creamy-french-lentils]] for the french-kit cousin and [[shittake-lentil-soup]] for the dark-stock sibling.

=== THE SHARED BACKBONE ===

- LENTILS (brown / spanish)
- MUSHROOMS (portabella — pureed or minced PER BUILD, see below)
- BUTTER for the sauté (no olive oil in the marmite build)
- ONIONS + GARLIC
- TOMATO PASTE (necessary but should NOT be tasted — the finished stew reads DARK, not red)
- WORCESTERSHIRE SAUCE (a great addition, frankly — primary in the stack)
- PORCINI POWDER (glutamates without tipping the scales)
- CUMIN
- ROSEMARY (thyme good too; BAY LEAF is the substitute if rosemary is unavailable)
- SALT + BLACK PEPPER

=== BUILD 1: THE MARMITE BUILD (the Jamie cottage-pie line — SERVED ON MASHED POTATOES) ===

- DICED onion + minced garlic + DICED/MINCED MUSHROOMS (NOT pureed — the chunk is nice; this build lacks vegetables and is a substantial dish, not a gravy), sautéed in BUTTER — no olive oil.
- GLUTAMATES: TOMATO PASTE + WORCESTERSHIRE + PORCINI POWDER + MARMITE — leaning MORE ON TOMATO, LESS ON MARMITE. NO DARK STOCK in this build (marmite + dark stock is too much MSG; tomato paste + marmite is all you need, like Jamie says).
- SEASONING: ROSEMARY + CUMIN + THYME (thyme is primary, but ROSEMARY IS MORE CRITICAL). CARAWAY stays OUT of this build — it turns horrible overnight here (fine in the ale build).
- ACID: a RELATIVELY GENEROUS amount of LEMON JUICE.
- THE FLAVOR ENGINE: CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON — lemon balances the rosemary and the marmite; cumin balances the lemon.
- POTATOES AS MASH, UNDERNEATH — the stew is served ON TOP of mashed potatoes, not with diced potato inside. The potatoes need to be there; mash is where they live.
- CELERIAC, TURNIPS, SWEDE/RUTABAGA secondary (they're in the Jamie Oliver). CARROTS and CELERY are CLASHING in this build. RED CHILI FLAKES secondary.
- BALANCE WARNING: sensitive to TOO MUCH FLAVOR INJECTOR OF ANY KIND — rosemary, marmite, and lemon all overshoot easily. Respect the engine.

=== BUILD 2: THE ALE + PICKLE BUILD (the pureed-mushroom gravy stew) ===

Built on the PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour), with DARK ALE + PICKLE JUICE + CUMIN/CARAWAY SEEDS doing the flavor injection.

1. SAUTÉ onions + garlic in BUTTER with the CUMIN and/or CARAWAY SEEDS blooming in the fat. (Add diced carrots/turnips here if using.)
2. PUREED MUSHROOMS: add the mushroom paste (food processor or blender) and cook it down.
3. FLOUR over the base, stir to coat (light roux).
4. DEGLAZE WITH DARK ALE (milk stout preferred — see BITTERNESS BUDGET note). Let it reduce briefly.
5. TOMATO PASTE + DARK BROTH + WORCESTERSHIRE: the vegetarian beef-stew backbone.
6. LENTILS in; simmer until tender (turnips soften alongside).
7. TANG: PICKLE JUICE to taste, then DICED DILL PICKLES. This is the register's balancer — NOT mustard or cream (see the kit note).
8. FINISH WITH SWEET PEAS, folded in at the end.
9. Serve as a stew; or top with mash + melting cheese and bake for the cottage-pie format (see PIE FORMAT note).

VEGETABLES in this build: ONIONS, PEAS, CARROTS, TURNIPS; LEEKS welcome (they bridge registers). HERBS: ROSEMARY (thyme also allowed) — fine herbs are clashing.
notes:
=== MERGED (2026-11-02): LENTIL COTTAGE PIE + MUSHROOM PICKLE RELISH → PUB STYLE LENTILS ===

The marmite line and the pickle line are one recipe now — the same anglo-dark pub register with one bitter-anchor slot, expressed as two builds. Everything from both files is preserved below; where the builds disagree (caraway, carrots, stock, mushroom texture, potato placement), the disagreement is BUILD-DEPENDENT, recorded per build.

=== ONE BITTER-ANCHOR SLOT — THE RULE THAT GOVERNS BOTH BUILDS ===

The dish has ONE bitter-anchor slot: MARMITE or DARK ALE (or dark stock, which became its own recipe — [[shittake-lentil-soup]]). NEVER STACK — marmite + dark stock was the single biggest balance failure (too much MSG, glutamate overload); stacking any two anchors overshoots the bitterness budget.

- MARMITE works in the cottage-pie build because ROSEMARY/THYME and the POTATO MASH back it up — the buffers absorb its intensity. In that build: NO dark stock; tomato paste + marmite is all you need, like Jamie says. Lean more on tomato, less on marmite.
- DARK ALE anchors the spare ale + pickle build — onions/lentils and not much else, so there aren't many buffers, and stock + marmite + tomato paste there is glutamate overload even for a chili-dog-like meal. MILK STOUT preferred — regular stout's bitterness compounds; milk stout's lactose sweetness keeps the budget in balance (the Nigella milk-stout-oxtail lesson). The dark bouillon in that build's gravy core rides UNDER the ale — it is not a second anchor.

=== THE GLUTAMATE STACK (MARMITE BUILD): TOMATO + MARMITE, NO DARK STOCK ===

THE MAJOR BALANCE PROBLEM, found: MARMITE + DARK VEGETABLE STOCK is just TOO MUCH MSG. You only need TOMATO PASTE and MARMITE (Jamie's Allotment Cottage Pie runs on the blended porcini/marmite/tomato-paste paste, no stock, no roux). PORCINI POWDER adds glutamates WITHOUT tipping the scales. WORCESTERSHIRE is a GREAT addition, frankly — primary in the stack. Butter only for the sauté — no olive oil.

=== THE FLAVOR ENGINE (MARMITE BUILD): CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON ===

CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON JUICE is a FLAVOR ENGINE and they all play well together: LEMON balances the ROSEMARY and the MARMITE, while CUMIN balances the LEMON. Use a relatively generous amount of lemon juice. If rosemary is unavailable, BAY LEAF is the most appropriate substitute. THYME is good and PRIMARY — but ROSEMARY IS MORE CRITICAL.

HARDEST TO BALANCE: sensitive to too much flavor injector of any kind — rosemary, marmite, lemon all overshoot easily. The biggest single culprit was stacking MARMITE + DARK STOCK; with the stock out and the engine balanced, it's much more nail-down-able.

(In the ale build, lemon is instead the RESCUE if over-spiced — lemon juice/zest pulls it back old-world; NOT ginger, wrong register.)

=== THE ANGLO-GERMANIC INJECTION (ALE BUILD) — ALE + PICKLE + SEED-SPICE ===

- DARK ALE: the bitter anchor (milk stout preferred).
- PICKLE JUICE + DICED DILL PICKLES: the register's tang. This is the german sour-into-the-braise logic (Linsensuppe's canonical vinegar finish, sauerbraten thinking) — pickle juice is vinegar with the dill axis pre-bundled. NOT mustard, NOT cream — those belong to the french kit (see BALANCER KITS below).
- CUMIN AND/OR CARAWAY SEEDS: the seed-spice bloomed in the butter. Cumin is the tested default; CARAWAY is the german cousin (carvone — the same aroma family as dill seed, so it harmonizes with the pickle axis at the molecular level). Either or both; SEEDS ONLY, never ground powder on top (over-spices).

=== CARAWAY IS BUILD-DEPENDENT — THE LEFTOVERS TEST ===

CARAWAY fits the ALE + PICKLE build (the carvone-dill harmony above) but is WRONG in the MARMITE build: it tasted OK in the pot, but OVERNIGHT IT JUST TURNED HORRIBLE — judge a stew by its leftover state, not its day-one state. CUMIN, on the other hand, is NECESSARY in both builds — a third of the marmite build's flavor engine, the bloomed seed-spice of the ale build.

=== BALANCER KITS ARE REGISTER-LOCKED ===

The french kit (wine/cream/mustard) and this kit (ale/pickle) don't cross. MUSTARD + MARMITE CLASH (confirmed by experiment). Mustard + ale is UNTESTED — flemish carbonnade (mustard melted into beer gravy) suggests it might coexist, so that edge stays open — but the working rule is: pick the register, use its kit.

=== MUSHROOM TEXTURE IS BUILD-DEPENDENT ===

- MARMITE BUILD: MINCED, not pureed — the CHUNK is nice in the final product, because the build lacks vegetables and it's a substantial dish, not a gravy.
- ALE BUILD: PUREED (food processor or blender) — the pureed-mushroom gravy core is the mechanism, shared with [[creamy-french-lentils]].

=== POTATOES — WHERE THEY LIVE PER BUILD ===

- MARMITE BUILD: AS MASH, UNDERNEATH. The potatoes NEED to be there, but the dish is better serviced ON TOP OF MASHED POTATOES — not with diced potato inside the stew. (The cottage-pie lineage, inverted — Jamie's original bakes the mash on top; here the stew rides over the mash.)
- ALE BUILD: no potato inside by default; the PIE FORMAT (below) is where the mash appears.

=== VEGETABLES PER BUILD ===

- MARMITE BUILD: spare on purpose. CELERIAC, TURNIPS, SWEDE/RUTABAGA secondary — might have misjudged them, frankly, because they're in the Jamie Oliver (the Allotment scaffold runs on swede + celeriac). CARROTS and CELERY are CLASHING in this build. RED CHILI FLAKES presumably good (secondary).
- ALE BUILD: ONIONS (base), sweet PEAS (folded in at the end — confirmed), CARROTS, TURNIPS (swede/rutabaga valid in the same slot). LEEKS welcome in both builds — they bridge the registers.

=== TOMATO — NECESSARY BUT SHOULDN'T BE TASTED ===

Tomato paste is part of the backbone in both builds, but the finished stew should read DARK, not red. In the ale build the PUREED MUSHROOMS + DARK ALE are the color-and-register blockers; note the ale build takes MORE tomato paste than the french sibling (the bitter base fights tomato, so it takes more to hold the warmth leg) even though it looks darker. Calibrate by register, not color.

=== HERBS — ROSEMARY; FINE HERBS CLASHING; FLORALS FAIL COLD ===

The herb slot is ROSEMARY/THYME ONLY. Fine herbs (parsley, basil, tarragon, fresh dill) are clashing. Floral dried herbs (coriander seed, herbes de provence) were tested and walked back — nice while hot, a tough sell once the dish COOLS, and this dish cools on the plate and reheats as leftovers as a matter of course.

=== PIE FORMAT (OPTIONAL) — THE COTTAGE LINEAGE ===

Both builds descend from cottage pie (via Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie — see REFERENCE below) and the ale build still takes the pie format when wanted: transfer the finished stew to a baking dish, top with mashed potatoes, bake ~20 min at 375°F, then scatter a MELTING cheese (cheddar or monterrey jack — not a hard grating cheese) and bake ~10-15 more until golden. As a stew it stands alone; the pie format is the presentation upgrade.

SERVING ALTERNATIVE — PIE, PEAS AND GRAVY: the northern-british pie-shop plate (mushy peas + gravy alongside/over) is the other format direction; the ale build currently takes its peas IN.

MARMITE-BUILD PAIRINGS: on mashed potatoes; pairs well with RICE and with PORK — less so with CHICKEN or HOT DOGS.

=== REFERENCE — VALIDATED EXPERIMENTS + JAMIE SCAFFOLD (READ-ONLY LOG) ===

The experiments that produced both builds remain valid; condensed:
- ORIGIN: reset onto Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie (root veg — leeks/carrots/swede/celeriac — + dried porcini + marmite + cumin seeds + crispy rosemary under mash; The Happy Foodie / Jamie's Veg). Cooked successfully as written. The two builds then departed in opposite directions: the marmite build kept his anchor and found the cumin+rosemary+lemon engine; the ale build swapped the anchor for stout and pickle tang.
- STOCK + VEGETABLES + GRAVY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — hearty stews need warmth (tomato paste + garlic) AND funkiness (marmite/worcestershire/ale) on top of stock.
- MARMITE CONFIRMED (second cook): bitterness/smokiness stock can't provide.
- MUSTARD + MARMITE CLASH (with the mustard+ale edge untested — carbonnade counterexample noted).
- CORIANDER: floral + bitter = double-clashing against the bitter anchor; herbes de provence's florals fail as the dish cools.
- CUMIN SEEDS ONLY, never ground cumin on top (over-spiced). Lemon juice/zest is the rescue if over-spiced (pulls it back old-world; NOT ginger — wrong register).
- DILL/PICKLE + BITTER: dill + tomato + pickle works when cumin + ale/marmite bitterness weighs it down — the refinement of the old hamburger-y hazard from the retired lentil wellington's spin-off era.
- ROOT VEGETABLES LIKE SPICE (turmeric in [[french-onion-vegetable-soup]], cumin here, cinnamon/nutmeg in [[root-vegetable-skillet]]); roots are the best vegetarian meat substitute at chunky cut.
- GERMAN CONVERGENCE: the sour-finished dark lentil stew is canonical german cooking (Linsensuppe, Swabian Linsen).
- Anglo spice cabinet still to explore: allspice (whole berries, not ground), mace, white pepper, mustard powder, molasses, malt vinegar, sage. The broader three-register theory lives in articles/stew-registers.md (read-only reference).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[creamy-french-lentils]]: the same gravy core with the french injection (mustard + cream + potato). The contrast pair.
- [[shittake-lentil-soup]]: the no-marmite, no-ale sibling — dark stock + tomato backbone, shiitake, clean build.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of this register (oxtail/short rib + milk stout + a dill pickle in the braise).
- [[braised-turnips]]: natural side; shares the turnip register.
- [[relish]]: the standalone condiment expression of the pickle-tang axis.

=== THE ROSEMARY RULE (UNSOLVED — FROM THE OLD STEW FAMILY) ===

ROSEMARY BELONGS WHERE A DARK ANCHOR LIVES — ale/marmite (this recipe, both builds) or dark stock ([[shittake-lentil-soup]]) — where it gives LIFT. In the celery + tomato forward stews ([[creamy-french-lentils]]; the retired italian mushroomed lentils) it tastes ORTHOGONAL. Competing theories: the dark anchor; 'something meaty'; or the CELERY itself — but [[chicken-pot-pie]] has celery AND rosemary happily, so no theory is clean. UNSOLVED. This recipe wants ROSEMARY.
original_chef: Both lines descend from Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie (Jamie's Veg, via The Happy Foodie): the marmite build is his cumin + marmite line; the ale + pickle build is mine, converged toward german Linsensuppe logic.
